message: I'm out delivering presents! Please leave a little space by the tree. My turning circle is ambitious.
Another chimney, another graceful entrance. Nobody needs to see the rehearsal footage.
The sleigh is full of Christmas magic. My pockets are increasingly full of biscuit crumbs.
I'm on my rounds! Rudolph is navigating and loudly reviewing the carrot selection.
Presents delivered, stockings filled, one squeaky floorboard successfully negotiated. Mostly.
I'm out and about spreading Christmas cheer. And a very small amount of chimney soot.
Quick postcard from the sleigh: all going well. My hat has only tried to escape twice.
The delivery team is flying along. The reindeer have requested that I stop singing directions.
I'm busy delivering your surprises. Head Elf says waving at every snowman is slowing us down.
Another stop ticked off! I'd stay for a chat, but there's a sackful of magic waiting.
Pacific deliveries are under way. I told Rudolph to watch the islands. He says he's watching all of them, which explains the weaving.
There's a lot of ocean between these stops. I've told the inflatable reindeer it's still only decoration.
The Pacific looks magnificent from up here. My map is mostly blue and one very important biscuit crumb.
I asked Head Elf for island-hopping tips. He said 'use the sleigh'. Excellent briefing.
Pacific route check complete. The presents are dry. My attempt to wave while drinking cocoa was less successful.
New Zealand on the route! I've told the sleigh this is a delivery run, not a scenic tour. It's taking its time replying.
The New Zealand parcels are ready. Rudolph has labelled his snack bag 'essential expedition equipment'.
I'm checking the next New Zealand stop. The elves packed a spare hat but no instructions for looking graceful.
Beautiful views on the New Zealand leg. I may have said 'ooh' over the radio more often than actual directions.
New Zealand delivery check: sack secure, boots ready, beard still trying to navigate independently.
Australian deliveries! I've loosened the scarf. Mrs Claus says that doesn't count as a summer wardrobe.
The Australian leg is a reminder that a red velvet suit was not designed by a weather expert.
I've packed extra water for Australia. Rudolph has packed extra opinions about my hat.
Australia on the map, parcels in the sack, sunglasses somewhere under thirty-seven gift tags.
The elves suggested lightweight boots for Australia. They sent my normal boots with fewer bells.
East Asia deliveries are under way. Head Elf has made the route book neat enough to frighten my handwriting.
I'm checking the next East Asian stop. Rudolph is checking whether my spare gloves contain biscuits.
The East Asia sack is perfectly organised. I have been asked not to 'improve' it.
A quick note from the East Asia leg: the ribbon has escaped again. It appears to be enjoying the journey.
East Asia route update: everything is on schedule, except my beard, which is still at the previous page.
Southeast Asia on the route. The scarf has officially requested reassignment to the luggage compartment.
The Southeast Asia parcels are ready. I've checked the tags twice and my snack pocket considerably more.
I'm following the Southeast Asia route notes. The cocoa ring around the important bit is entirely my contribution.
Southeast Asia delivery duty: one cheerful Santa, eight focused reindeer and a very warm hat.
A quick pause on the Southeast Asia leg to straighten the sack. The teddy bears have voted against my parking.
South Asia deliveries are under way. Head Elf has put the instructions in large print. A subtle message.
Checking the South Asia parcels. One toy drum has been auditioning for the sleigh orchestra all night.
The South Asia route book is open. So is the biscuit tin. I can multitask when properly motivated.
A note from the South Asia leg: I have found my glasses. They were helping hold my hat on.
South Asia delivery check complete. The spare ribbon is now a belt, which was not in the original plan.
Central Asia on the route. There's plenty of room on the map, but somehow none in my pockets.
The Central Asia sack is ready. Rudolph says the route would be simpler if I stopped pointing with a biscuit.
I'm checking the Central Asia leg. The compass is fine; my sense of where I put it needs attention.
Central Asia deliveries: beautiful views, careful navigation and one very determined loose jingle.
A quick postcard from the Central Asia leg. I asked for silence while I read the map. Eight reindeer sighed in unison.
The Middle East parcels are ready. My sunglasses have finally justified their place in the emergency kit.
Middle East route check: water packed, scarf loosened, hat still refusing all practical suggestions.
I'm following the Middle East delivery notes. Head Elf has underlined 'do not stop to polish the bells'.
A quick message from the Middle East leg: the sleigh is running beautifully. I am running mostly on snacks.
Middle East deliveries are under way. The elves have labelled my cocoa 'Santa fuel'. Very professional.
European deliveries are under way. The route book has more tabs than Head Elf's computer.
The Europe sack is ready. I've put my spare gloves somewhere sensible, which means they're lost.
Europe on the route! I asked the satnav for festive directions. It has added a jingle to every turn.
Checking the next European stop. Rudolph says my 'shortcut' looks suspiciously like a bakery detour.
A quick postcard from the Europe leg. My boots are quiet. Unfortunately, the knees supplied their own sound effects.
African deliveries are under way. I've promised the team this is not the moment for another hat adjustment.
The Africa sack is ready. Head Elf has counted the parcels; I've counted the emergency biscuits. Both vital.
Africa on the route. I'm admiring the view while Rudolph reminds me that admiring isn't a navigation method.
A quick note from the Africa leg: the sleigh is sparkling. I suspect the elves used the fancy polish.
Checking the next African stop. The presents are beautifully wrapped. The same cannot be said for my scarf.
South American deliveries are under way. The sack is organised and I have been told to leave it that way.
The South America route notes are ready. Head Elf has drawn a tiny warning beside my proposed snack stops.
South America on the map. Rudolph is flying beautifully; I'm trying to unfold a map without wearing it.
A quick postcard from the South America leg. The view is spectacular. The photograph is mostly mitten.
Checking the next South American stop. The toy parrot keeps repeating my directions. We now have two navigators.
Central America deliveries! The route is carefully planned. My pocket full of crumbs is entirely spontaneous.
The Central America parcels are ready. I've checked every bow, including the one accidentally tied to my sleeve.
A quick note from the Central America leg: Rudolph has requested a co-pilot who doesn't point with snacks.
Central America on the map. Head Elf says my handwriting looks like sleigh tracks. I call it branding.
Checking the next Central American stop. The sack is getting lighter and my emergency biscuit supply agrees.
North American deliveries are under way. There's a lot of map left, but Rudolph has his determined ears on.
The North America sack is ready. I've been practising my quiet landing face. It looks suspiciously like panic.
North America on the route! Head Elf has reminded me that 'roughly over there' is not a coordinate.
A postcard from the North America leg: the sleigh is doing brilliantly. My hat is clinging on for the credit.
Checking the next North American stop. The last toy robot has offered to drive. I've declined politely.
Antarctic research-station deliveries! Finally, weather that understands my choice of coat.
Antarctica on the route. I waved at a penguin. No reply. Clearly a very serious member of staff.
The Antarctic parcels are ready. Rudolph says this is the first time all night he hasn't questioned my scarf.
A quick Antarctic note: lovely scenery, excellent coat weather, absolutely nowhere to hide a bright red sleigh.
Delivering to the Antarctic research stations. I've asked the scientists whether they can explain where my spare glove went.
UK parcels ready. I've put the kettle on my mental checklist. Mrs Claus says it's not a delivery stop.
The UK leg is going well. I'm resisting the urge to judge every chimney's architectural merits.
France on the route. I packed a phrasebook, but somehow every page now opens at 'pastry'.
The French parcels are ready. My attempt at an elegant entrance was undermined by a squeaky boot.
Germany on the route. Head Elf has made a very precise schedule. My biscuit breaks are being reviewed.
The German parcels are sorted. I asked for a festive flourish; the elves gave my clipboard a bow.
Japan on the route. I've checked the gift tags twice. The toy robot has checked my work and looks smug.
The Japanese parcels are ready. Rudolph has politely requested that I stop narrating every turn.
Australia on the route. I suggested shorts with the red coat. Mrs Claus ended the video call.
The Australian parcels are sorted. I've marked my sunglasses 'not a present' after last year's near miss.
New Zealand on the route. I packed a camera for the views. The memory card is already full of beard.
The New Zealand parcels are ready. I told Rudolph to make a grand entrance. He suggested a careful landing instead.
USA parcels ready. I've checked the route twice and the size of my snack supply three times.
The United States leg is going well. The sleigh has cup holders; I consider that essential expedition planning.
Canada on the route. My spare mittens are enjoying their moment of professional relevance.
The Canadian parcels are ready. I asked Rudolph for a smooth landing. He asked me to sit still for once.
Brazil on the route. The sleigh bells have started a rhythm and I'm under strict instructions not to dance at the controls.
The Brazilian parcels are sorted. My cheerful wave nearly became an unscheduled glove delivery.
South Africa on the route. I've remembered the sunglasses and forgotten which pocket contains them.
The South African parcels are ready. Rudolph says my hat adjustment has become a full-time occupation.
